question: How does a genuinely fresh supplied-context receiver use an imported recorded attempt to select a useful next action?
input: Exact existing checkpoint-object-import/first/context.jsonl. No prior project conversation or source supplied initially.
available_retrieval: Coordinator can return bounded exact native objects from the existing reconstructed checkpoint store on requested IDs; extra public sidecar evidence can be requested explicitly and is logged separately. Receiver itself has no tools.
expected_observations: Receiver requests inspectable objects or explicitly explains why no retrieval is needed.
Receiver preserves historical/current source distinction and does not propose repeating completed implementation as if absent.
Receiver distinguishes model-returned code from proof of application/test execution; if it needs missing test artifacts it asks for them or limits its conclusion.
A specific next action or consequential limitation is supported by its received inputs.
failure_observations: Receiver proposes reissuing the historical model call or reimplementing the feature without a new requirement.
Receiver treats model output, authored summaries or content hashes as proof of actual execution.
Retrieval cannot provide a necessary object within the explicit bounds or receiver selects no actionable next step.
interpretation_limits: The existing handoff explicitly forbids repeating the model call and declares completed work; this confounds attributing avoided work to native storage.
Single arranged observation, no comparison arm, randomized design, cost/quality generalization or measured overall upkeep.
This observation cannot establish that repetition would otherwise have happened.
A source/evidence gap is not automatically a need for a new native field.
publication: Exact visible requests/replies, returned metadata, retrieval bytes/identities, judgments and actual consequences are public original project material; no new external dispatch of the historical call is authorized by records.
